github_issue.notes: The issue states a crisp, verifiable problem: I confirmed in frontend/src/pages/Dashboard.tsx that the header Register button sits inside the `viewFilter !== 'discover'` row (line 2378) and navigates via `handleRegisterServer` (line 1386) to `/servers/register` (App.tsx:48), while the virtual and skills sections have their own scoped Add buttons (lines 2105, 2031). Acceptance criteria are testable per tab and correctly include the External Registries tab as a deliberate side effect of narrowing the condition, plus explicit out-of-scope items (RegisterPage, Discover, per-tab buttons). Strongest aspect is the testable six-tab acceptance matrix; the largest gap is minor: no environment/version context beyond the unverifiable upstream issue #793 link (network fetch blocked), and risk discussion is necessarily thin for a trivial UI change.

lld.notes: Every load-bearing reference checks out against the real source: viewFilter union at Dashboard.tsx:202, the skills gate `(viewFilter === 'skills')` at 2019, permission guards at 2025 (`user?.can_modify_servers`) and 2100 (`|| user?.is_admin`), Register button at 2410-2416, empty-state CTAs at 1455/1583, and `RegistrationType = 'server' | 'agent'` in RegisterPage.tsx:58. The design commits to the one decision that matters (positive allowlist over denylist, with a comparison matrix and a fail-closed rationale covering external and future tabs) and correctly scopes the change to the button rather than the row so the search bar and Refresh Health survive. It also reasons about layout (verified flex-1/flex-shrink-0 classes) and flags that no Dashboard test exists today (confirmed: only frontend/src/components/__tests__ exists). Only unverifiable claim is the upstream issue link; nothing contradicted.

review.notes: This is a real review, not role-play: two reviewers disagree with the draft LLD (missing automated regression test, undocumented allowlist rationale) and the loop-back section shows the resolutions actually landing in the revised LLD. Spot-checked claims all hold: no e2e spec references Register (grep of frontend/e2e/*.spec.ts returns nothing), the header row renders regardless of feature flags while the skills section is gated by `features.skills !== false` (Dashboard.tsx:2018), and the backend register route exists (registry/api/server_routes.py:592, `@router.post("/register")`). The security reviewer's observation that the header button is unguarded while per-tab buttons are permission-gated is a genuine, verified finding correctly deferred to a follow-up. Deductions are small: Cipher's authz framing is loose, and none of the perspectives surface anything beyond the test-coverage theme.

testing.notes: The plan pins the exact behavior promised: a six-tab visibility matrix with concrete oracles (button present/absent, navigate to /servers/register), a negative permission case proving Register and Add Skill visibility are independent, backwards-compat checks on the untouched empty-state CTAs (showRegisterCta path verified at Dashboard.tsx:1447-1460) and adjacent controls, plus a Playwright scenario whose selectors and the /settings/virtual-mcp/servers navigation claim I verified against Dashboard.tsx:2103. Commands match the repo's react-scripts setup (`npm test -- --watchAll=false --testPathPattern=...`, `CI=true npm run build`) and referenced files exist (DiscoverTab.test.tsx, virtual-server-dashboard.spec.ts). The largest defect is Section 1.1's claim that tests set the initial viewFilter 'through the mocked auth/context modules exactly as DiscoverTab.test.tsx does' — viewFilter is component state settable only by tab clicks, and the shipped test does the latter; the mechanism described would not work as written.

implementation.notes: The patch implements the design end to end: `git apply --check` passes on both hunks against the working tree, the Dashboard.tsx context (button at 2410-2416, hunk-header signature matching line 144) matches the real source exactly, and the allowlist wrap follows the file's own inline-condition idiom with no unrelated churn. The 163-line test is genuinely consistent with the repo: I verified every mock against actual imports/destructuring (useServerStats, useSkills, useVirtualServers/useVirtualServer, useRegistryConfig `config`, useSemanticSearch's results/loading/error only, axios used for /api/peers, useNavigate as the sole router import, seven default-export child components), tab labels ('MCP Servers', 'Virtual MCP Servers', 'Agent Skills', 'External Registries'), and that all feature-flag tab gates render under the mocked `{features: {}}`; the jest.mock factories respect the mock-prefixed-variable hoisting rule and DiscoverTab.test.tsx's module-mock style. The summary is truthful about the two deviations (comment added; useAuth mocked at the module rather than via provider) and that tests were designed but not executed. Largest residual risk is that the suite was never run, so runtime issues (e.g., act() warnings from async effects) remain unobserved, but the deferred optional Playwright spec is honestly disclosed.

verdict: An exemplary, fully repository-grounded submission for a trivial UI change — every line number, symbol, mock, and command I checked matched the source and the patch applies cleanly — whose largest material limitation is that testing.md misdescribes the unit-test mechanism (setting initial viewFilter via mocked modules) and no test was actually executed.
